identity.name: Ziyarid dynasty
alt_names: Ziyarid state of Gilan and Tabaristan

land.text: Asfar's former territories, 'which included Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj'

predecessors.note: Mardavij defeated and killed Asfar in 931 and became ruler of his lands (Mardavij page). Asfar has no dossier or Cliopatria row (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

land.text: Hamadan, Dinavar, Kashan and Isfahan, the 'Abbasid cities' Mardavij captured after 931, and Ahvaz (Khuzestan) by 934

predecessors.note: Mardavij's conquests of 931-934 (Mardavij page). Fars (Shiraz) only acknowledged his authority under Ali ibn Buya (vassal, 934-935) and is not Ziyarid land.
Makan ibn Kaki held Tabaristan from 930 and most of Gurgan (Mardavij page); Mardavij took Tabaristan in 932. Cliopatria's Zaydi row runs to 935.

land.text: Tabaristan, Gilan and Gorgan, 'invaded and conquered' in 1090

successors.note: No dossier or Cliopatria row exists for the Nizari Ismaili state of Alamut; it needs one (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

capitals.name: Ray (Rey)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ray (935-943)'. Vushmgir was crowned in Ray (Ziyarid page); Ray was lost for good in 943 and briefly occupied again in 958.

capitals.name: Gorgan
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gorgan (943-1035)'. The narrative contradicts it in places: Makan held Gorgan from 936, al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan held Gorgan and Tabaristan until 947 (Vushmgir took Gorgan briefly in 945), the Buyids took both in 948 and they 'changed hands several times until 955', so Gorgan was not held in 943-946 (Vushmgir was with the Bavandids and at the Samanid court) nor in 948-954; held in exile by the Buyids 980/981-998.

rulers.name: Bisutun (Zahir al-Dawla)
rulers.note: The caliph gave him the title Zahir al-Dawla in 971.

rulers.name: Qabus, second reign
rulers.note: Table 997-1012; the text says he returned in 998; overthrown by his army in 1012.

rulers.name: Manuchihr (Falak al-Ma'ali)
rulers.note: Recognised the sovereignty of Mahmud of Ghazni.

rulers.name: Anushirvan (Sharaf al-Ma'ali)
rulers.note: Table 1030-1050, overlapping Manuchihr by a year; accepted Seljuq authority 1041/42.

correction.text: Mardavij's realm in 931: Gilan; Asfar's former lands 'Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj' (drawn as Rey, Qazvin and Zanjan); and the Abbasid cities Hamadan, Dinavar, Kashan and Isfahan (capital)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Ziyarid shape begins in 936, after Mardavij's death. 'In 931, Mardavij managed to defeat and kill Asfar'; he 'became ruler of Asfar's former territories, which included Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj' (no year of its own) and took 'the Abbasid cities of Hamadan, Dinavar, and Kashan, and finally, Isfahan', his capital. The region is the researcher's reading of the city and province names (confidence 2): Qom and Karaj are inside no province drawn here; Gilan is the dynasty's homeland, not named as held on the Mardavij page. The page gives no area.

correction.text: The 931 realm plus Tabaristan (conquered 932 from Makan ibn Kaki) and Gurgan (Golestan), which Mardavij ceded to the Samanids in 933 and so held

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'conquered Tabaristan in 932' (lead). Gurgan is the researcher's inference (confidence 2): the page has Makan 'extended his rule over most of Gurgan' (930) and Mardavij 'agreed to cede Gurgan to the Samanids' in 933, but does not say that the 932 conquest took it.

correction.text: The 932 realm without Gurgan, ceded to the Samanids in the peace of 933; Ray was held 'for tribute' to the Samanids

keyframe_review.note: 'In 933, Mardavij made peace with the Samanid ruler Nasr II' and 'agreed to cede Gurgan to the Samanids and pay tribute for his possession of Ray'. Ray stays Ziyarid land under Samanid tribute.

correction.text: Mardavij's peak: the 933 realm plus Khuzestan (Ahvaz); Fars (Shiraz) only acknowledged his authority under Ali ibn Buya and is not drawn as Ziyarid land (vassal 934-935)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'By 934, his authority was acknowledged as far as Shiraz and Ahvaz'; 'his troops managed to conquer as far as Ahvaz' (after the 933 peace, no year of its own) and forced Ali, 'who was now in Shiraz', to 'once again acknowledge his authority'. The Ziyarid page says 'At its greatest extent, it ruled much of present-day western and northern Iran'. Khuzestan is the researcher's reading of Ahvaz (confidence 2). Fars was Buyid land: the Buyid dossier founds there in 934.

correction.text: Vushmgir's realm in 935: the north (Gilan, Tabaristan, Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan) and Gorgan, which he 'wrested from Samanid control'; the central and southern possessions went to the Buyids

keyframe_review.note: 'Mardavij's brother Vushmgir succeeded him in northern Iran'; Ali ibn Buya 'had taken over Mardavij possessions in central and southern Iran' (Mardavij page); Hasan ibn Buya 'seiz[ed] Isfahan from Ziyarid rule' (Ziyarid page, no year). Gorgan: the Ziyarid page says Vushmgir, crowned in Ray, 'then wrested Gorgan from Samanid control' (no year; before the 936 turn-over to Makan): confidence 1.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 936 Tabaristan shape plus Ray (Vushmgir's capital 935-943), valid 936-942; the shape alone is the next keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 40,543 km2 for 936-969 (Mazandaran 85 cells, Gilan 30, Semnan 11, Qazvin 10, Tehran 9, Golestan 2 on the gazetteer): the Tabaristan and Gilan core. It lacks Ray ('Ray (935-943)' in the infobox; 'Ray was lost for good in 943, to the Buyid Hasan') and Gorgan (given to Makan in 936). The page gives no area. Right for 936-942 with Ray; the later keyframes (943, 944-946, 947, 948-954, 955-969) override it. Ray was also lost briefly c. 940: Abu 'Ali Chaghani, after the siege of Gorgan (939 or 940), 'engaged Vushmgir in battle in Ray and defeated him, killing Makan', and Vushmgir 'retook control of Ray' when Chaghani left for Khurasan (no years): not drawn, gap.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 936 shape unchanged for 943 only: Tabaristan and Gilan without Ray (lost to the Buyid Hasan in 943)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe splitting the 936-969 shape: the years change, not the shape. After losing Ray Vushmgir went back to Tabaristan, where al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan defeated him (no year; placed in 944).

correction.text: empty: Vushmgir held no land. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan held Tabaristan and Gorgan; Vushmgir 'fled to the Bavandids of the mountains in eastern Tabaristan, then to the court of the Samanid Nuh I' and 'in 945 ... captured Gorgan with Samanid support, but did not manage to retain his rule there'

keyframe_review.note: Replaces the earlier 943-946 keyframe, which drew the Tabaristan core as Ziyarid while the page has al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan holding Tabaristan and Gorgan until 947. Gilan is not mentioned for these years; nothing a page gives Vushmgir is drawn (the 945 capture of Gorgan is brief and is the contest, not a shape). The empty correction resolves to no cells by design.

correction.text: Tabaristan and Gilan plus Gorgan (Hyrcania) for 947 only: 'in 947 ... take Gorgan and Tabaristan from al-Hasan with the help of a large Samanid army'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the retaking of 947 from al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan, not from the Buyids; in 948 the Buyid Hasan (Rukn al-Dawla) 'invaded Tabaristan and Gorgan and took them from Vushmgir'. Gorgan's east edge is beyond Cliopatria's bbox (54.2 E).

correction.text: empty: 'In 948 Hasan (Rukn al-Dawla) invaded Tabaristan and Gorgan and took them from Vushmgir'; they 'changed hands several times until 955' while Vushmgir 'relied on his Samanid allies' - drawn as the contest of 948-955, not as Ziyarid land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page does not say who held either land in any of these years, only that they changed hands; the dossier therefore draws no Ziyarid shape and lets the 948-955 contest show the blend (the Buyid dossier should hold the 948 gain). The earlier keyframe drew Tabaristan and Gorgan as Ziyarid throughout 947-969. Resolves to no cells by design.

correction.text: Tabaristan and Gilan plus Gorgan (Hyrcania), valid 955-969: in the Samanid-brokered treaty of 955 Rukn al-Dawla 'promised to leave Vushmgir alone in Tabaristan'; the Buyid counterattacks of 960, 962 and 966 gave only brief gains (the contest of 960-966)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Vushmgir's brief occupation of Ray in 958 is an occupation event, not part of the shape. Gorgan is included although the treaty names only Tabaristan: Rukn al-Dawla's 960 counterattack is described as 'temporarily taking Gorgan', which implies Vushmgir held it.

41,018 km2 for 970-979: the same Tabaristan and Gilan core as 936 (bbox 49.1-54.2 E), without Gorgan. Bisutun (967-977) took the title Zahir al-Dawla from the caliph in 971; Qabus ruled from 977 and was 'expelled in 980' (the next keyframe). The page gives no area.

correction.text: empty: no Ziyarid land 980-997; 'The Buyids now dominated Tabaristan over 17 years while Qabus was in exile in Khorasan' (Tabaristan 980 and Gorgan 981 on the Buyid dynasty page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the dynasty is in exile, not extinct (Qabus returns 998 and the line continues to 1090), so the dossier stays open and draws nothing for these years. Cliopatria ends the row in 979.

correction.text: Tabaristan, Gilan and Gorgan under Qabus (returned 998), Manuchihr, Anushirvan, Keikavus and Gilanshah, vassals of the Ghaznavids from 1012 and the Seljuqs from 1041/42

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria lacks (the row ends in 979). The Qabus page says 'Supporters of the Ziyarid gained control of Tabaristan and from there conquered Gurgan' (998) and gives no description of the extent of the state after that; it names neither Gilan nor Amol as held. The Ziyarid page names the rulers and the 1012, 1035, 1041/42 and 1090 events but no frontier. The extent is therefore the earlier core (including Gilan, unverified) with Gorgan: confidence 2 for 998-1034 and 1 afterwards (the capital moves from Gorgan to Amol in 1035 and 'the Ghaznavids ... sacked the Ziyarid capital of Amol'). The infobox gives no area.

region.text: Gilan, the Ziyarids' homeland, and Isfahan, Mardavij's capital 931-935

ledger.note: 931: Mardavij founds the Ziyarid state at Isfahan. Infobox 'Established: 931' and 'Isfahan (931–935)'; the text calls the dynasty 'an Iranian dynasty of Gilaki origin that ruled Tabaristan from 931 to 1090'. The table says 930 and the header '928–1043', which the page does not explain.

931: Mardavij takes the Abbasid cities of the Jibal. After defeating and killing Asfar in 931 he began 'capturing the Abbasid cities of Hamadan, Dinavar, and Kashan, and finally, Isfahan' (Mardavij page, no year of its own); the Ziyarid page says he captured them from the Abbasids. The year is Asfar's death. Asfar's own lands are the next event.

region.text: Asfar's former territories: Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj

ledger.note: 931: Mardavij defeats and kills Asfar and takes his lands. 'In 931, Mardavij managed to defeat and kill Asfar' and 'became ruler of Asfar's former territories, which included Ray, Qazvin, Zanjan, Abhar, Qom and Karaj' (no year of its own for the take-over); Qom and Karaj are not drawn.

932: Mardavij conquers Tabaristan. 'He then defeated the Daylamite military leader Makan ibn Kaki, and conquered Tabaristan in 932' (another sentence of the page dates the personal conquest to 931; in 930 Makan had 'briefly recover[ed] Tabaristan' from the Zaydi domain Asfar had invaded). Cliopatria's Zaydi Alid row runs to 935.

932: Gurgan passes to Mardavij with Tabaristan (inference). Makan 'extended his rule over most of Gurgan' in 930 and in 933 Mardavij 'agreed to cede Gurgan to the Samanids', so he held it; the page does not say the 932 conquest took it.
933: Mardavij cedes Gurgan to the Samanids. 'In 933, Mardavij made peace with the Samanid ruler Nasr II': he ceded Gurgan and paid tribute for Ray.

934: Mardavij's troops reach Ahvaz. 'By 934, his authority was acknowledged as far as Shiraz and Ahvaz' (lead); the body says 'his troops managed to conquer as far as Ahvaz' after the 933 peace, without a year, and does not say whose Ahvaz was; the Ziyarid page lists Ahvaz among the cities taken from the Abbasids. Khuzestan is the researcher's reading. Fars is the next event.

934: Ali ibn Buya in Shiraz acknowledges Mardavij. Mardavij 'forced Ali, who was now in Shiraz, to once again acknowledge his authority' (no year of its own; the lead's 'By 934' covers it). Fars is Buyid land (the Buyid dossier founds there in 934), here a client.

region.text: Mardavij's possessions in central and southern Iran, less Fars

ledger.note: 935: the Buyids take Mardavij's central and southern possessions. 'In January 935, shortly before Nowruz festivities, Mardavij was assassinated by his Turkic slaves'; Ali ibn Buya 'had taken over Mardavij possessions in central and southern Iran' (Mardavij page, no year of its own) and Hasan ibn Buya seized Isfahan 'from Ziyarid rule' (Ziyarid page, no year). Fars was never Ziyarid land (vassal until the next event).
935: Mardavij's death ends the Buyid acknowledgement. Ali 'founded the Buyid dynasty' after the assassination of January 935 (Mardavij page; the Buyid dynasty page has 934 for the founding in Fars).

c. 935: Vushmgir takes Gorgan from the Samanids. The Ziyarid page says he, crowned in Ray, 'then wrested Gorgan from Samanid control' (no year); it follows the accession of 935 and precedes the turn-over to Makan in 936.
935: Vushmgir rules from Ray. Infobox 'Ray (935–943)'; 'Mardavij's brother Vushmgir succeeded him in northern Iran' (Mardavij page).

936: Vushmgir turns Gorgan over to Makan. 'He soon decided to acknowledge Samanid supremacy, and in 936 turned Gorgan over to Makan.' Vushmgir is a Samanid vassal from here (an event for the Samanid dossier).
938: Vushmgir retakes Isfahan. Hasan 'retook Isfahan in 940', after Vushmgir had retaken it in 938.
940: the Buyid Hasan retakes Isfahan from Vushmgir ('retook Isfahan in 940').
943: Ray is lost to the Buyids. 'Ray was lost for good in 943, to the Buyid Hasan.'

943: the capital is Gorgan (infobox 'Gorgan (943-1035)'); the narrative has Makan, al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan and the Buyids holding Gorgan in 936-947 and 948-954, so the infobox date is the page's and the residence is not borne out.

c. 944: al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan defeats Vushmgir in Tabaristan. After Ray was lost in 943, 'Returning to Tabaristan, he was defeated there by al-Hasan, who had previously occupied Gorgan'; Vushmgir fled to the Bavandids and then to the Samanid court (no year on these sentences: placed between 943 and 945). Al-Hasan was the governor of Sari who had revolted against Vushmgir and 'supported the Buyids'; he is not the Buyid Hasan.

945: Vushmgir's campaign for Gorgan begins. 'In 945 Vushmgir captured Gorgan with Samanid support, but did not manage to retain his rule there'; al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan, who 'had previously occupied Gorgan', held Gorgan and Tabaristan until 947.

947: Vushmgir takes Gorgan and Tabaristan from al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan. 'It was only in 947 when he was able to take Gorgan and Tabaristan from al-Hasan with the help of a large Samanid army' (Vushmgir page: he 'managed to defeat al-Hasan and expel him from Tabaristan'). Not taken from the Buyids.
947: the contest with al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan ends with his expulsion from Tabaristan and Gorgan.

948: the Buyid Hasan takes Tabaristan and Gorgan. 'In 948 Hasan (who since the Buyids' entrance into Baghdad in 945 had used the title Rukn al-Dawla) invaded Tabaristan and Gorgan and took them from Vushmgir' (also on the Vushmgir page). Mirror event for buyid-dynasty (me-08-c).

948: the Buyid invasion begins a struggle for Tabaristan and Gorgan. Vushmgir 'relied on his Samanid allies' while al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan supported the Buyids; the lands 'changed hands several times until 955'.

955: a Samanid-brokered treaty ends the first round. 'Tabaristan and Gorgan changed hands several times until 955, when in a treaty with the Samanids, Rukn al-Daula promised to leave Vushmgir alone in Tabaristan.'

955: Vushmgir holds Tabaristan and Gorgan again. The page does not say he recovered them, only that the treaty left him 'alone in Tabaristan'; the 960 counterattack is described as 'temporarily taking Gorgan', which implies he held it. Mirror event for buyid-dynasty (me-08-c).
958: Vushmgir briefly occupies Ray ('briefly occupied Ray').

958: the occupation of Ray ends in the same year (assumed). The Ziyarid and Vushmgir pages say only that Vushmgir 'briefly occupied Ray' and that 'Rukn al-Dawla later made a counter-attack' - no year, no month.

960: Rukn al-Dawla's counterattacks begin. 'Temporarily taking Gorgan in 960, then Tabaristan and Gorgan for a short time in 962' and 'may have also taken Tabaristan and Gorgan in 966' (Vushmgir page); the gains were brief, so the land stays Ziyarid in the shape.

966: the last Buyid counterattack. Rukn al-Dawla 'may have also taken Tabaristan and Gorgan in 966, but did not hold on to them for long'; Vushmgir was killed by a boar in December 967 (Vushmgir page), shortly after a Samanid army arrived for a joint campaign against the Buyids.

980: the Buyids take Tabaristan. The Buyid dynasty page lists 'Tabaristan (980)' among Adud al-Dawla's additions; the Ziyarid page has Qabus 'expelled in 980' and 'The Buyids now dominated Tabaristan over 17 years while Qabus was in exile in Khorasan'.
981: the Buyids take Gorgan ('Gorgan (981)' on the Buyid dynasty page; Qabus's first reign is listed 977-981).

998: Qabus returns. 'Qabus returned there in 998' and 'Supporters of the Ziyarid gained control of Tabaristan and from there conquered Gurgan' (Qabus page; the Ziyarid page also has 'In 998, Qabus returned to Tabaristan'; its rulers table has the second reign from 997). The Buyids had held Tabaristan since 980.
1035: the capital is Amol. Infobox 'Amol (1035–1090)'; 'In 1035, Abu Kalijar stopped paying tribute to the Ghaznavids, and the Ghaznavids sacked Amol'.

1090: the Nizari Ismailis end Ziyarid rule. 'In 1090, the Nizari Ismaili state invaded and conquered his domains, which ended Ziyarid rule in Tabaristan' (Gilanshah, last ruler 1087-1090). The Ziyarids were Ghaznavid vassals after 1012 and Seljuq vassals after 1041/42.

wars.name: Conquests of Mardavij
wars.outcome: Mardavij killed Asfar (931) and took his lands and the Abbasid cities of the Jibal, conquered Tabaristan (932), made peace with the Samanids in 933 ceding Gurgan, and by 934 was acknowledged as far as Shiraz (Ali ibn Buya, a client) and Ahvaz.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of the Ziyarid south
wars.outcome: After Mardavij's murder in January 935 Ali ibn Buya took his possessions in central and southern Iran and Hasan ibn Buya seized Isfahan; Vushmgir retook Isfahan in 938 and lost it again in 940.

wars.name: Samanid, Buyid and Fairuzanid wars for Ray, Gorgan and Tabaristan
wars.outcome: The Samanid governor Chaghani attacked Gorgan in 939/940 and defeated Vushmgir at Ray; Ray fell to the Buyid Hasan in 943; al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan, Vushmgir's rebel governor of Sari, took Tabaristan and Gorgan and was expelled only in 947 by a Samanid army (Vushmgir held Gorgan briefly in 945); Rukn al-Dawla invaded in 948 and the lands changed hands until the treaty of 955 left Vushmgir alone in Tabaristan; he occupied Ray briefly in 958; Buyid counterattacks followed in 960, 962 and perhaps 966 with brief gains.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Tabaristan and Gorgan
wars.outcome: Qabus was expelled in 980 and fled to Khorasan; the Buyids held Tabaristan (980) and Gorgan (981) until he returned in 998.
wars.note: The Ziyarid page does not date Gorgan's loss.

wars.name: Ghaznavid and Seljuq overlordship
wars.outcome: Manuchihr 'quickly recognized the sovereignty of Mahmud of Ghazni' in 1012; in 1035 Abu Kalijar stopped paying tribute and the Ghaznavids sacked Amol; the Seljuqs 'forced him to accept their authority' in 1041/42.
wars.note: No territorial change is dated; the relations are the overlords' vassal events.

wars.name: Nizari Ismaili conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: The Nizari Ismaili state invaded and conquered Gilanshah's domains in 1090, ending Ziyarid rule.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded: the Daylam and Tabaristan hill frontiers, the Samanid peace of 933 (Gurgan) and the 955 treaty name regions, not lines; the empty spans 944-946, 948-954 and 980-997 have no frontier.

sources.title: Ziyarid dynasty
sources.note: Identity, infobox (931-1090, capitals), rulers table, Vushmgir's wars 935-967 (re-read 2026-10-20 for al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan, 947, 948, 955, 958, 960-966), Qabus, Ghaznavid and Seljuq overlordship, 1090.

sources.title: Mardavij
sources.note: The founder's conquests 930-934 (re-read 2026-10-20): Asfar and his lands 931, the Abbasid cities, Tabaristan 932, the 933 peace and Gurgan, Ahvaz and Shiraz by 934, murder January 935.

sources.title: Buyid dynasty
sources.note: Opened for the Hamdanid dossier of this batch; used here only for 'Tabaristan (980)' and 'Gorgan (981)'.

sources.title: Vushmgir
sources.note: Vushmgir's reign: 943 Ray, 945 Gurgan, 947 expulsion of al-Hasan, 948 Buyid invasion, 955 treaty, 958 Ray, Buyid counterattacks 960/962/966; the flight to Tabaristan and the revolt of al-Hasan ibn al-Fairuzan are undated.

sources.title: Qabus
sources.note: Qabus: exile to 997, return in 998 to Tabaristan and conquest of Gurgan, death 1012; no description of the state's extent after 998.

notes: Row question (data/README): none; Cliopatria's 'Ziyarid dynasty' (936-979, two near-identical shapes of about 41,000 km2, Mazandaran, Gilan and slivers of Qazvin, Tehran and Semnan) is the Tabaristan core only. It misses Mardavij's 931-935 empire (new keyframes 931 and 934), Ray in 935-942, Gorgan from 947 and the years 998-1090 in which the dynasty ruled Tabaristan as a Ghaznavid and then Seljuq vassal (Cliopatria ends the row in 979, the page in 1090); the dossier therefore runs 931-1090 with an empty exile keyframe 980-997. Page budget 1-2 (Ziyarid dynasty; Mardavij), plus the Buyid dynasty page already opened for another dossier. The Ziyarid page's own dates disagree: infobox 931, rulers table 930 (Mardavij) and header '928-1043'; Qabus returned 997 (table) or 998 (text); Gorgan was capital from 943 though it changed hands in 936, 945 and 947. Who held Gorgan and Tabaristan in 943-946 is not settled (the Buyids, to judge from 947): confidence 1. Vassal relations are the overlords' events and are not repeated as ledger events: Samanid suzerainty from 936 (and tribute for Ray from 933), Ghaznavid suzerainty from 1012 (Manuchihr), Seljuq authority from 1041/42; the ghaznavid-empire, samanid-empire and great-seljuk-empire dossiers should carry vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart ziyarid-dynasty. The Zaydi Alid row (866-935), Makan ibn Kaki and Asfar ibn Shiruya are the predecessors on the page; the Nizari Ismaili state (successor in 1090) has no dossier. Gazetteer: 'Hyrcania' stands for Gorgan with Tabaristan, 'Rey' for Ray, 'Golestan' for Gurgan; Dinavar and Kashan are covered by the Kermanshah and Esfahan provinces; none is missing.
